definitions.explanation: A place where trains or buses stop for passengers.

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}の{駅|えき}で{降|お}りる。
examples.english: I'll get off at the next station.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}の{前|まえ}に{大|おお}きい{店|みせ}がある。
examples.english: There is a big shop in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}は{駅|えき}に{人|ひと}が{多|おお}くて、{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}るのが{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: In the morning there are a lot of people at the station, so it's hard to get on the train.

examples.japanese: この{駅|えき}から{学校|がっこう}まで{電車|でんしゃ}で{三|さん}つ{目|め}だから、{毎朝|まいあさ}{同|おな}じ{時間|じかん}に{家|いえ}を{出|で}る。
examples.english: My school is three stops from this station by train, so I leave home at the same time every morning.

notes:
{駅|えき} refers to train and bus stations.

COMPOUNDS:
- {駅前|えきまえ}: area in front of the station
- {駅員|えきいん}: station staff
- {終着駅|しゅうちゃくえき}: terminal station
- {乗り換え駅|のりかええき}: transfer station

COMMON STATIONS:
- {東京駅|とうきょうえき}: Tokyo Station
- {新宿駅|しんじゅくえき}: Shinjuku Station
